Glorieth
glo'ri-eth
v. (boasts, exults; the archaic third person of glory, and the hinge of Jeremiah's rule that Paul quotes twice)
From Latin gloriari, to boast, from gloria, glory, through Old French. The Authorized Version's -eth ending is the ordinary third-person singular of 1611. The Hebrew at Jeremiah 9:24 is halal, to praise or boast; the Greek at 1 Corinthians 1:31 is kauchaomai.

Biblical Definition

Jeremiah lays down a rule that governs the whole doctrine of boasting: “Thus saith the LORD, Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches” (Jeremiah 9:23) — and then, rather than forbidding boasting altogether, redirects it: “But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the LORD which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the LORD” (Jeremiah 9:24). Three grounds of pride are named — wisdom, might, riches — and each is a thing men actually possess; the objection is not that the boast is false but that the ground is wrong. Paul quotes the rule twice, and both times as the conclusion of an argument about the humbling of human pride: “He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord” (1 Corinthians 1:31; 2 Corinthians 10:17). In the first he has just said that God chose the foolish, the weak, and the base things of the world, that no flesh should glory in his presence. The doctrines of election and of grace alone are not abstractions; they exist in Scripture in this practical form, to put an end to boasting.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) gives glory as a verb meaning to boast, to be proud of, and notes that in a good sense it is to rejoice or exult in what is right.

expand to see more

GLORY, v.i. To boast; to be proud of; to be vain of; to exult with joy.

No one should glory in his prosperity.

2. To rejoice; to be proud of, with a good sense; as, to glory in the cross of Christ.

GLORYING, n. Boasting; a boast or vaunt.

GLORY, n. Praise ascribed in adoration; honor and admiration.

Key Scripture

Jeremiah 9:24 — "But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the LORD which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the LORD."

Jeremiah 9:23 — "Thus saith the LORD, Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches:"

1 Corinthians 1:31 — "That, according as it is written, He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord."

2 Corinthians 10:17 — "But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord."

Modern Corruption

The rule is read as a ban on all confidence, or ignored entirely in a ministry culture built on visible achievement.

expand to see more

Jeremiah 9:23-24 is misread in both directions. Some take it as forbidding any satisfaction in any thing, producing a false humility that cannot receive a gift or acknowledge a mercy — which is not the text, since the LORD does not abolish the boast but assigns it an object. Others quote the verse and then build ministries on precisely the three grounds it names. Wisdom, might, and riches are the currencies of contemporary religious influence as surely as they were of Jerusalem's, and a movement can affirm sola gratia in its statement of faith while running entirely on platform, reach, and budget.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; the corruption is the perennial one of the human heart. The principle to recover is the object. What a man glories in reveals what he trusts, and Jeremiah names the permitted ground with great precision — not that I am saved, and not that I am right, but that he understandeth and knoweth me, and specifically knows the LORD as one who exercises lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness in the earth. That is a boast in God's character, made by a man who has been given to know it. Paul's use in 1 Corinthians 1 ties it directly to election: God chose as He did so that no flesh should glory in His presence.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew halal, to praise or boast — Jeremiah 9:23-24; Greek kauchaomai, to boast — 1 Corinthians 1:31, 2 Corinthians 10:17; Latin gloriari, to boast.

expand to see more

Hebrew halal — to shine, to praise, to boast; the root also of hallelujah. Jeremiah 9:23-24.

Greek kauchaomai — to boast or exult; 1 Corinthians 1:31 and 2 Corinthians 10:17, both quoting Jeremiah.

Greek kauchema — the ground of boasting; Romans 4:2, where Abraham has none before God.

Latin gloriari, from gloria — the source of the English verb.

The -eth ending is simply the 1611 third person singular, as doeth, saith, knoweth.

Usage

"“Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom” — three real possessions, three wrong grounds."

"“He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord” — Paul quotes the rule twice."

"“That no flesh should glory in his presence” — the pastoral point of election."
